hints.content: The numerator of $~\dfrac{{{5}^{n}}}{n!}~$ is an exponential function, and the denominator is a factorial function. The factorial function grows at a faster rate than any exponential function.  To see this, imagine letting $~n=100\,$.  The numerator would have $~100~$ factors of $~5\,$.  The denominator would also have $~100~$ factors, but $~95~$ of those factors would be larger than $~5\,$.

As $~n\to \infty~$, the denominator grows at a much faster rate than the numerator.  

Hence,$\qquad\displaystyle\underset{n\to \infty }{\mathop{\lim }}~\frac{{{5}^{n}}}{n!}=0\,$.
